paper_metadata.title: Accelerating the design of multivariate Nb-Si based alloys with excellent strength and toughness matching through machine learning

evidence.quote: The applications of Nb-Si-based alloys for new-generation engines are heavily influenced by their strength and toughness.
the generalization ability was proved by the Nb-16Si-20Ti-xB4C (x = 0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.0 at%) alloys fabricated in previous work

the RF and KNN prediction models were used for the alloying design of five-element Nb-(16 20) Si-(20 24) Ti-(0 6) Al-(0 6) Cr alloys (at%) with compositions ranging from hypoeutectic to hypereutectic zones.
Nb-16Si-24Ti-3Al-6Cr alloy with excellent strength and toughness matching was selected as the optimal material from 1225 candidate materials.

process_steps.input_state: Nb, Si, Ti, Al, and Cr elemental powders

evidence.quote: The powders were weighed according to the selected composition proportion and then ball milling for 6 h.
The powder mixture was pressed into cylinders with a diameter of 10 mm and a height of 10 mm under a pressure of 10 MPa.

the ingots were fabricated in a non-consumable copper crucible under an argon atmosphere (DHL400). ... The alloy ingot was remelted five times to ensure uniformity, and the weight loss rate was less than 0.5 wt%.

By adding alloying elements to adjust the composition, content, and size of the Nb-based solid solution (Nbss) and silicide phases ((α, β, γ)-Nb5Si3 or/and Nb3Si), and form a small amount of Laves phase Cr2Nb, Nb4Fe3Si5 (depending on the alloy system), the strength and toughness matching of Nb-Si-based alloys can be optimized.

machine_learning_models.name: Random Forest Regression
machine_learning_models.task: predict fracture toughness of Nb-Si-based alloys from alloying element compositions
machine_learning_models.dataset: 259 arc-melted Nb-Si-based alloy samples with fracture toughness data

evidence.quote: The result indicated that Random Forest (RF) and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) regression models were suitable for predicting Nb-Si-based alloys’ fracture toughness and compressive strength, respectively
